text:
samir: quick ping, found a reproducible phase flip when reinserting a short SYS token on q3-int3 hybrid during long generates
jess: which model/build?
samir: magnet-13b-q3-int3hyb, seq=32k. baseline fp32 ok. q3 shows divergence ~6.1k tokens after reinject.
aline: any kernel flags? rotary_rescale? pack_stride?
samir: rotary_rescale=on reduces freq but doesn't remove. pack_stride seems related.
jess: paste minimal repro and logs?
samir: repro steps: run 8k token generation, at t=2k insert {"role":"system","content":"NOTE\n"} then continue. curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"magnet-13b-q3","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"INIT\n"},{"role":"user","content":"<long>"}],"stream":false }'
# programmatically inject system message mid-run
```
samir: key snippet from canary logs: 
[2026-03-25T11:11:02Z] kv_pack_index: 1510
[2026-03-25T11:11:02Z] kv_pack_stride: 64
[2026-03-25T11:11:02Z] rope_base: 0x9f2d -> 0x9f1f (delta -14)
[2026-03-25T11:11:02Z] top_logit: "ing" vs expected "ed"

aline: delta -14 again. hypothesis: small-write pack alignment causes a shift in anchor mapping for some heads due to integer rounding in packed offsets.
jess: tests to run: (1) pad reinjection to full stride boundary, (2) force anchor_recompute after reinject, (3) run with prefix_cache_disable=true. compare top-5 logits pre/post.
samir: I ran (1) and (3): padding to stride boundary mostly fixed it, prefix_cache_disable also fixes.
ci-bot: ci: magnet-13b-q3-anchorpatch canary built and deployed to pool-7
jess: good signal. add instrumentation: head_phase_checksum and top10 logits snapshot at +/-50 tokens of injection. also add quant4-hybrid run and dedicated GPU run.
aline: if confirmed fix: allocator should keep stable offsets for tiny inserts or we need a lightweight re-anchor after any midstream prompt insertion. add regression in longcontext-suite.
samir: filing issue ML-11729 and attaching logs. will run multi-trial overnight and post results.
jess: thanks, keep us posted. :gear:
